claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response of as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons is governed by the density and nature of magnetic domain boundaries and interfacial defects.
Low-dimensional processing accentuates interfacial defects in FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons.
Interfacial defects act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Domain-wall pinning suppresses the effective magnetocaloric response.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi has inherent nanoscale heterogeneity and a high interfacial-defect density.
Rapid thermal annealing below the onset of phase change is the proposed controlled intervention.
Rapid thermal annealing will reduce or reconfigure interfacial defects and domain-wall pinning sites.
Pinned domain walls have higher energy barriers for magnetic-domain reorientation.
Domain-wall pinning slows magnetic response during low-field cycling.
Annealing-mediated defect healing or domain-boundary reconfiguration will enhance domain-wall mobility.
Annealed samples should have a smaller hysteresis-loop area than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples should exhibit a higher or sharper magnetocaloric peak than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing-induced defect clustering could produce the opposite magnetocaloric and hysteresis changes.
The proposed pinning mechanism should dominate at low magnetic fields and cycle frequencies for which heat transfer is limiting.
The applicable operating-temperature window is near room temperature.
No systematic hysteresis reduction or no corresponding domain-structure reconfiguration after annealing is proposed as a falsification result.
